chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Zayd al-Qurashi, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'When Allah causes the inhabitants of the earth to die, He causes the inhabitants of the lowest heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the second heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the third heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the fourth heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the fifth heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the sixth heaven to die, then He causes the inhabitants of the seventh heaven to die. Then He causes Mikail to die — he said, or Jibrail — then He causes Jibrail to die, then He causes Israfil to die, then He causes the Angel of Death to die. Then the Horn will be blown and they will be resurrected.'

Then Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will ask, 'To whom does the Kingdom belong this Day?' Then He will respond Himself saying, 'To Allah, the Creator, the Originator, and the Fashioner; and Exalted is Allah, the One, the Subduer.' Then He will ask, 'Where are the tyrants? Where are those who called upon another god besides Me? Where are the arrogant ones?' — and similar to this — then He will resurrect the creation.

key_terms.الْخَالِقُ الْبَارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ: The Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner
key_terms.لِمَنِ الْمُلُكُ الْيَوْمَ: To whom belongs the Kingdom today?

ai.seo_question: What is the sequence of death and resurrection for the heavens, angels, and creation according to Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* outlines the cosmological dismantling of the universe, emphasizing the sequential death of the seven heavens' inhabitants and the archangels, a detail that highlights the transient nature of all created beings except Allah. The subsequent rhetorical question, 'For whom is the dominion today?', directly echoes the Quranic declaration of absolute sovereignty, serving as a theological refutation of polytheism and arrogance by affirming Allah as the sole King and Judge. In Shia tradition, this sequence underscores the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the ultimate humiliation of the *Jabbarun* (tyrants) who claimed divinity or equality with God.
